label: accepted

evidence.V1: Octagonal token reads instantly front and three-quarter; outline is symmetric (A15 X/Y 0.0); top view is the expected chunky gold edge bar, still reads as a coin edge-on; silhouette is a clean solid polygon.
evidence.V2: Big (thick gold rim) and medium (recessed teal field + raised octagon boss) are clear, but there is no small-tier detail: the boss is a blank plate with no emblem/inset, so the face reads sparse at close range.
evidence.V3: Confident chunky stylised proportions: thick rim (~0.28 stud deep on 1.5 stud face), deep recess and stubby boss read as a toy token, not a stiff primitive.
evidence.V4: Even small chamfers on the rim's inner/outer edges and on the boss catch a light highlight in the rim close-up; bevel width looks consistent across parts.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups clean: no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray faceting on the recess floor, boss or rim; gate A17/A18 zero overlaps/flips.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: kit gold rim + one hue (teal) in two-three values (dark field, lighter boss); colourways (crimson, shadow) keep the same value structure.
evidence.V7: 192 tris vs small-class target 600 / ceiling 1500, economical with no wasted loops.
evidence.V8: Single white LF_VertexColor material, gold accent + one hue, chamfer scale and smooth shading match the kit coin anchor.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

top_fixes: Add a small-tier emblem or inset on the octagon boss (e.g. raised cream glyph or stepped inner bevel) to complete the big/medium/small hierarchy
Optionally add a thin inner lip/step on the rim inner wall to break up the large flat teal field
